To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) derived datatypes in MPI can be used to improve performance of communication of noncontiguous memory regions, (2) derived datatypes can be optimized for memory-access efficiency by using packing algorithms, (3) packing algorithms can be automatically generated by a compiler, (4) the performance of the optimized derived datatypes can significantly exceed the performance of the existing MPI implementations.

the performance of MPI-derived datatypes can be improved by optimizing for memory-access cost and that our implementation of MPI-derived datatype outperforms manual packing by the users and existing derived-datatype implementation in MPICH.

the memory-access cost of a communication can be significantly reduced by optimizing the memory layout of data before sending or receiving it, that this optimization can be done automatically by the MPI implementation, and that this approach significantly improves the performance of derived-datatype communication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
optimizing the performance of derived data types.
improving the performance of MPI by optimizing the memory-access cost of derived datatypes.
improving performance of derived datotypes in MPI by using memory optimization techniques that the user does not have to know or implement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our implementation of MPI derived datypes significantly outperforms manual packing by the users and the existing implementation of MPI derived data type in MPICH.
the proposed approach is an effective way of optimizing the memory access of derived datatypes.
the performance of the derived datatype is significantly improved by using memory-optimized packing algorithms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new MPI implementation that is faster than the current best MPI implementations on the same hardware.
the derived datatypes are not a bottleneck in the communication performance of the MPI implementation.
we have implemented a derived datatype library in MPICH that outperforms the existing MPICH derived datatypes and the manual packing of data by users.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MPI Standard can be implemented in such a way that it provides significant performance benefits over manual packing by the programmer.
the performance of derived types is not limited by the communication cost but by the cost of accessing the memory of the noncontiguous data.
it is possible to improve derived datatypes significantly by applying memory-optimization algorithms that are optimized to the memory architecture of the underlying machine.
